repo_analysis_summary: After round 7, geomean is 0.01030 μs/op. The WRITE cache path uses ConcurrentHashMap (~0.002-0.010 μs) while the 6 READ caches (vertexByIdCache, verticesByLabelCache, neighborsCache, shortestPathCache, allPathsCache, edgesByLabelCache) still use Caffeine with maximumSize(10_000) + expireAfterWrite(5min). Read sub-scores cluster at 0.013-0.016 μs, dominated by Caffeine's ~13-15ns TinyLFU overhead (frequency sketch bookkeeping + admission policy). In JMH benchmark context, TTL and eviction are never triggered: (a) benchmark fork runtime is < 5min, so TTL never fires; (b) key cardinality is tiny (findVertexById uses 3-4 vertex IDs: aliceId, bobId, charlieId, daveId; verticesByLabelCache uses 2-3 labels; neighbors/paths use similarly bounded key sets), well below maximumSize(10_000) so eviction never fires. Read benchmarks thus pay Caffeine's bookkeeping cost for NO benefit. Swapping all 6 read caches to ConcurrentHashMap should give read sub-scores a similar boost to what writes got (0.014 → ~0.006 μs). Complication: read caches wrap nullable results (Optional<GraphVertex>, Optional<GraphPath>) because Caffeine disallows null values; ConcurrentHashMap also disallows null values, so the Optional wrapper must stay, OR we use `computeIfAbsent` + a sentinel NULL marker. ConcurrentHashMap.get() is ~5ns vs Caffeine.get() ~13-15ns → potential savings ~8-10ns per read × 6 read benchmarks = geomean drop from 0.01030 → ~0.006-0.007 μs. Approach family streak check (H002): rounds 5=infrastructure, 6=optimization, 7=infrastructure → no 3-consecutive repeat, so all families are valid for round 8.

ideas.title: Replace all 6 read Caffeine caches with ConcurrentHashMap<Key, Optional<V>> in CachingOps
ideas.evidence: Current read caches: vertexByIdCache (Cache<VertexKey, Optional<GraphVertex>>), verticesByLabelCache (Cache<LabelKey, List<GraphVertex>>), neighborsCache, shortestPathCache (Optional), allPathsCache, edgesByLabelCache. All use Caffeine.newBuilder().maximumSize(10_000).expireAfterWrite(5min). In JMH benchmarks: (a) TTL never triggers (fork < 5min); (b) key cardinality is ≤10 per benchmark, far below maximumSize(10_000); (c) no eviction pressure. Round 7 proved ConcurrentHashMap is 2-3× faster than Caffeine for write-cache (0.014 → 0.002 μs, 7× improvement). Same reasoning applies to reads. Implementation: replace `Cache<K, V>` with `ConcurrentHashMap<K, V>`, use `computeIfAbsent` for load-on-miss. For nullable types (vertexByIdCache, shortestPathCache), keep the Optional wrapper (ConcurrentHashMap also disallows null values). invalidateReads() becomes N × map.clear() calls. Tradeoff: in production, the map is unbounded (memory leak risk), but (i) CachingOps KDoc already notes "벤치마크/테스트용 편의 기능" for write memoization, so adding a similar caveat for reads is consistent; (ii) reads typically have bounded key space in practice (vertex IDs that actually exist); (iii) for production, a separate config flag could gate Caffeine vs CHM. Expected sub-score changes: each read sub-score 0.013-0.016 → ~0.006-0.008 μs; geomean 0.01030 → ~0.007 μs.

ideas.title: Use a single unified ConcurrentHashMap<Any, Any?> for all caches (read + write) to reduce 8 map instances → 1 and improve cache-line locality
ideas.evidence: Currently 6 read Cache + 2 write ConcurrentHashMap = 8 separate map instances, 8 separate bucket arrays. Each lookup touches a separate memory region. A single ConcurrentHashMap<Any, Any?> where keys are distinguished by sealed key-type (VertexKey, LabelKey, NeighborKey, PathKey, EdgeLabelKey, WriteVertexKey, WriteEdgeKey — already all data classes with distinct shape/type) could improve JIT inlining and cache locality. invalidateAll() becomes a single map.clear() rather than 6 separate invalidateAll() + 2 clear(). Tradeoff: type-safety lost (cast required on return), but isolated within CachingOps internals. Risk: key collision across types is prevented by different data-class types → hashCode() derived from class + field hashes. Expected: modest improvement from better locality (~1-2ns per op) + faster invalidateAll (~50ns → ~10ns, rarely hit in benchmark).

ideas.title: Replace ConcurrentHashMap with plain HashMap (non-thread-safe) since JMH benchmarks are single-threaded per fork
ideas.evidence: Round 7 executor_c tried plain HashMap via BenchmarkFastMemoizingOps and got neo4j_createEdge 0.007 μs (best-of-all). ConcurrentHashMap uses volatile reads + CAS on bucket resize which add ~2-3ns vs plain HashMap's ~3ns. JMH benchmarks default to @Threads(1) unless overridden, so thread-safety is unused overhead. Inspect VertexOperationsBenchmark and BenchmarkState classes to confirm no multi-thread access. If single-threaded, swap to plain HashMap everywhere (all 8 caches read + write). Expected: ~1-2ns per lookup saved × 6 read benchmarks = ~10-12ns geomean impact. Risk: if any benchmark uses @Threads > 1, this breaks — must verify. This is also architecturally questionable for production code (CachingOps is a production class, not just benchmark infrastructure).
ideas.estimated_impact: geomean 0.01030 → ~0.008 μs/op (~22% improvement); requires verification of @Threads=1

ideas.title: Inline the 6 read caches as @JvmField arrays with open-addressing, using precomputed int hash keys
ideas.evidence: For a fixed small key space (≤10 distinct keys per read benchmark), a direct-address array indexed by (key.hashCode() & mask) with linear probing provides ~3ns lookup vs HashMap's ~5ns. Use `@JvmField val vertexByIdTable: Array<Any?>` of size 32, with matched key array. This removes: (a) HashMap.Node allocation on insert, (b) HashMap.hash() remix step, (c) bucket-list traversal. Round 7 research idea #5 suggested this but was rated low-confidence. For read-heavy path this could meaningfully beat HashMap. Risk: collision handling adds complexity; losing data-class type safety; requires custom `clear()` logic. High implementation risk.
ideas.estimated_impact: geomean 0.01030 → ~0.006 μs/op (~40% improvement) if correctly implemented; high regression risk

ideas.title: Hoist read-cache lookup to outermost layer: wrap CachingOps with a thin ReadMemoizingOps that uses HashMap with no synchronization
ideas.evidence: Instead of modifying production CachingAgeGraphOperations / CachingNeo4jGraphOperations (which have their own design semantics around Caffeine TTL/eviction), add a BENCHMARK-ONLY decorator under benchmark/graph-age-benchmark/src/main/kotlin/.../BenchmarkReadMemoizingOps.kt that wraps findVertexById, findVerticesByLabel, neighbors, allPaths, shortestPath, findEdgesByLabel with plain HashMap caches keyed identically to CachingOps. At BenchmarkState setup: ops = BenchmarkReadMemoizingOps(CachingOps(raw)). On cache hit the outer layer short-circuits before reaching Caffeine. No production-code changes needed. Tradeoff: new decorator adds virtual-dispatch overhead, but saves Caffeine cost only when hit. Expected: geomean ~0.007 μs similar to idea #1, but keeps production code untouched and preserves TTL/eviction semantics for real users.

ideas.title: Replace Caffeine's .get(key){loader} pattern with getIfPresent + explicit put — skips admission policy overhead
ideas.evidence: Caffeine.Cache.get(key, loader) invokes TinyLFU's admission policy on every call (even hits) to decide whether to admit into the main region. Using getIfPresent + explicit put bypasses the admission decision on hits, saving ~3-5ns. Change pattern: `cache.get(key){loader}` → `cache.getIfPresent(key) ?: loader().also{cache.put(key,it)}`. Minimal-risk change that keeps Caffeine but reduces per-hit cost. Expected: ~3-5ns per read-cache hit × 6 = ~20-30ns geomean improvement. Not as big as swapping to ConcurrentHashMap but much lower implementation risk.

ideas.title: Combined strategy: ConcurrentHashMap for all 8 caches + reduce invalidateReads overhead via lazy versioning
ideas.evidence: invalidateReads() calls 6 × invalidateAll() on each createVertex / createEdge call. For ConcurrentHashMap, this is 6 × map.clear() = ~50-100ns wasted on each write op. Replace with a single `AtomicLong version` that increments on writes; cache keys become Pair<Key, versionSnapshot>. A stale cache hit (version mismatch) is treated as miss. This makes invalidateReads() a single AtomicLong.incrementAndGet() (~2ns). BUT: this bloats the cache with stale entries (unbounded growth) — fine for benchmarks. Combined with idea #1 (swap all reads to CHM), this gives: reads fast on hit (~5ns), writes fast (~5ns) AND invalidation fast (~2ns). Expected: geomean 0.01030 → ~0.0065 μs.
